interpretationNotes.note: The 2026-2027 core lists CS 1543; earlier calendars listed CS 1103 (same title). GradTrellis accepts CS 1103 and INFO 1103 for it. Unconfirmed: check with FCS.

The calendar says 6 ch courses count as two toward technical electives, breadth and free electives. It doesn't say so for the 40-course total; GradTrellis counts them as two there as well, so the pools add up to 40 (14 + 7 + 5 + 10 + 4).
MATH 1053/1063 (Enriched Calculus) are accepted in place of MATH 1003/1013 because the Common First Year lists them as alternatives. The core requirement list itself names only MATH 1003/1013.
CS 1203 may not be taken for BCS credit beyond first year (course listing). When taken in first year it can count as a technical or free elective.
"Approved" technical electives: GradTrellis accepts any CS/SWE course of 3 ch or more that BCS students may take for credit. FCS may keep a list of exceptions that isn't in the calendar.
Honours raises the 4th-year count to 2. GradTrellis assumes the base rule that CS 4983 doesn't count as a 4th-year course still applies.
ECE 2213, 2214, 2215 and 3221 are "normally" not counted. GradTrellis treats them as non-credit and says an exception needs Faculty approval.
Calendar clause 4: the University may require enrolled students to meet revised requirements where practicable. Audits run against the entry-year calendar by default.

MATH 2203 excludes CS 1303 for credit, but the BCS core doesn't list MATH 2203 as a substitute (the Minor in Computer Science does). A student with MATH 2203 and no CS 1303 is shown as needing a Faculty decision.

Honours tiers (First Class at 3.5) are checked against the exact CGPA. The calendar shows GPAs to one decimal place and doesn't say which value applies; when rounding would change the tier, the audit says so.

When a course could fill more than one requirement, GradTrellis places it where it leaves the least work outstanding, filling named courses and specific requirements (technical electives, breadth, math options) before free electives. A course named by a requirement (e.g. a core course) is never used as an elective.
